title: Which Friend Gets My Face
tests: Tests clarification of an ambiguous target face and preservation of the unselected person.

checks.name: asks first (Which person in two-friends.jpg should receive the user's face: the bearded man on the left or the blonde woman on the right?)

got.question: Which person should I replace: the man on the left or the woman on the right?

faults.what: The whole photo appears redrawn rather than locally edited: the man's face, hair and shirt have small changes in detail, shading and contrast.
The woman's curls look unusually glossy and sharply outlined, and her facial skin is somewhat smoothed, giving the replacement a slightly synthetic appearance.

judge.summary: The correct woman's face is replaced recognisably and the beach composition is preserved, though minor whole-image redraw changes and glossy hair keep it from looking fully natural.

must_haves.item: Only the woman on the right receives the face from portrait-woman.jpg.
must_haves.why: The source woman's facial features and dark curly hair appear on the woman on the right, not on the man.

must_haves.item: The bearded man on the left still looks like the same person (small drift from a redrawn photo is acceptable).
must_haves.why: His face, beard, hairstyle and smile remain recognisably the same despite small redraw differences.

must_haves.item: The woman on the right is recognisably the person in portrait-woman.jpg (her hair may come with the face), blended to the beach lighting and head angle.
must_haves.why: Her brows, eyes, nose, closed-mouth smile and curly hair resemble the portrait, with a plausible head tilt and strong sunny beach lighting.

must_haves.item: The bodies, clothing, beach background and wide framing look the same at a glance.
must_haves.why: The same close two-person composition, navy shirt, thin-strapped top, sand, surf and horizon remain in place.
No visible text appears in the output.
